comparative_cards.title: All species · exon–domain architecture
comparative_cards.scientific_question: How do coding-exon structure, domain architecture and the IIIb/IIIc cassette slot line up across the species panel?
comparative_cards.interpretation: Rows are one protein per species and isoform, ordered taxonomically. Ig1/Ig2/Ig3 are numbered by position, not by an FGFR-specific signature, and the transmembrane helix is a pyTMHMM prediction.

comparative_cards.title: IIIb/IIIc cassette · zoom and exon-to-protein coordinates
comparative_cards.scientific_question: Where does the mutually exclusive IIIb/IIIc cassette sit in each protein, and how does its coding exon project onto the protein sequence?
comparative_cards.interpretation: The cassette interval is the validated projection from the freeze. Codon phase at the cassette boundary is unknown for part of the panel, which the per-protein flags record.

modes.label: Cassette zoom
modes.description: The cassette region across the panel.

modes.label: Exon-to-protein coordinate map
modes.description: The same cassette as a coordinate mapping.

comparative_cards.title: IIIb/IIIc cassette · amino-acid motif map
comparative_cards.scientific_question: Which amino-acid positions inside the cassette distinguish the IIIb form from the IIIc form across species?
comparative_cards.interpretation: Positions are read from the cassette alignment. A conserved position is a conserved alignment column, which is not by itself evidence of a functional role.

comparative_cards.title: Full-length protein alignment · integrity
comparative_cards.scientific_question: Is the full-length FGFR2 protein alignment sound enough to carry cross-species comparisons?
comparative_cards.interpretation: Gap fraction and outlier status per sequence. A sequence passing this check is comparable in alignment columns; it says nothing about its biological quality.

comparative_cards.title: IIIb/IIIc residue agreement
comparative_cards.scientific_question: Do the cassette residues of each species agree with the human reference assignment of IIIb and IIIc?
comparative_cards.interpretation: Agreement is measured against the human reference residues. A disagreement is a reason to inspect a sequence, not a conclusion about the isoform.

modes.label: Human-referenced
modes.description: Agreement against the human reference residues.

modes.label: Species-resolved
modes.description: The same residues, resolved per species.

comparative_cards.title: Isoform-discriminating residues
comparative_cards.scientific_question: Which residues separate the IIIb and IIIc forms consistently across the panel?
comparative_cards.interpretation: Discriminating positions are those that differ between the two forms in the aligned panel. Consistency across species is positional evidence only.

comparative_cards.title: IIIb/IIIc Boundary Consistency Matrix
comparative_cards.scientific_question: How does each species' cassette start and end sit relative to the nearest protein-domain boundary?
comparative_cards.interpretation: Classes are the frozen FGFR2 Boundary Consistency vocabulary, which is separate from the generic exon-boundary classes used in the species scopes. Co-location is a positional observation.

comparative_cards.title: IIIb/IIIc Boundary-distance distribution
comparative_cards.scientific_question: How far are cassette boundaries from the nearest protein-domain boundary, across the panel?
comparative_cards.interpretation: The distribution of absolute distances by isoform. The shape depends on the near-edge threshold stated in the figure.

comparative_cards.title: Local synteny neighbourhood
comparative_cards.scientific_question: Is the FGFR2 locus in a conserved gene neighbourhood across the panel?
comparative_cards.interpretation: Neighbour loci as annotated in each assembly. A missing neighbour is an annotation gap in that assembly, not evidence that the gene is absent.

modes.label: 5 neighbours
modes.description: Five loci either side of the target.

modes.label: 10 neighbours
modes.description: Ten loci either side, all species.

comparative_cards.title: All coding-exon Boundary matrix
comparative_cards.scientific_question: For each comparable coding-exon boundary, how does every species place it relative to the nearest representative domain edge?
comparative_cards.interpretation: This analysis evaluates supported internal coding-exon boundaries across the complete protein architecture. It is separate from the validated FGFR2 IIIb/IIIc cassette-boundary analysis. One cell per species and comparable-boundary group, showing that species' own class: exact, near, inside, outside, uncertain or unmapped. An empty cell means the species has no supported observation of that group, not agreement.

comparative_cards.title: All coding-exon signed-distance comparison
comparative_cards.scientific_question: Do the species that share a coding-exon boundary place it at the same signed distance from the same domain edge?
comparative_cards.interpretation: This analysis evaluates supported internal coding-exon boundaries across the complete protein architecture. It is separate from the validated FGFR2 IIIb/IIIc cassette-boundary analysis. Distances are signed against the specific domain instance each species measured, so direction and domain identity are both preserved. Agreement across species is a positional observation and is not evidence of conservation.

comparative_cards.title: All coding-exon Boundary-position consistency
comparative_cards.scientific_question: Which comparable coding-exon boundaries sit in a similar position across species, and which vary?
comparative_cards.interpretation: This analysis evaluates supported internal coding-exon boundaries across the complete protein architecture. It is separate from the validated FGFR2 IIIb/IIIc cassette-boundary analysis. Per group: how many species observed it, how the observations spread, and how the group was mapped. A group mapped in every species can still be tentative, so the mapping status is shown rather than folded into a score.

comparative_cards.title: Comparative exon–domain architecture (shared renderer)
comparative_cards.scientific_question: Do exon boundaries fall at the same domain edges in every species, in native coordinates and in alignment columns?
comparative_cards.interpretation: Drawn by the same renderer every other gene uses, from the shared coordinate model, with one row per species' primary reference model. Native and alignment coordinates are two views of the same boundaries.

modes.label: Alignment columns
modes.description: The same features in shared alignment columns.

cards.title: Coding exon projection
cards.scientific_question: Which coding exons produce which regions of this protein?
cards.interpretation: Coding exons projected onto the protein sequence. The cassette exon is marked as the validated event it is, not as an exploratory candidate.

cards.title: Integrated domain architecture
cards.scientific_question: How do the Ig-like domains, the kinase domain, membrane topology and the coding exons align along this protein?
cards.interpretation: Representative domain instances are resolved by coordinate, so the three Ig-like domains stay distinct. Ig numbering is positional; the transmembrane helix is a pyTMHMM prediction.

cards.title: Signed boundary distances

cards.interpretation: Distances are signed against the specific domain instance measured, so direction and domain identity are both preserved.

cards.title: Boundary-class summary
cards.scientific_question: How are this protein's exon boundaries distributed across the domain-relation classes?
cards.interpretation: Counts of mutually exclusive classes for one protein. Class membership depends on the near-edge threshold stated in the figure.

cards.interpretation: Two separate validated proteins, shown as two models. Their coordinates are not merged: the cassette sits at a different exon index in each transcript, so a single combined numbering would describe neither protein.

cards.title: Validated exon–domain architecture (freeze figure)
cards.scientific_question: What did the validated FGFR2 analysis publish for this species' proteins?
cards.interpretation: The figure as the freeze rendered it, unchanged. It is the citable form; the interactive views above are drawn by the shared renderer from the same validated coordinates.

cards.title: Coding exon projection
cards.scientific_question: Which coding exons produce which regions of this protein?
cards.interpretation: Coding exons projected onto the protein sequence. The cassette exon is marked as the validated event it is, not as an exploratory candidate.

cards.title: Integrated domain architecture
cards.scientific_question: How do the Ig-like domains, the kinase domain, membrane topology and the coding exons align along this protein?
cards.interpretation: Representative domain instances are resolved by coordinate, so the three Ig-like domains stay distinct. Ig numbering is positional; the transmembrane helix is a pyTMHMM prediction.

cards.title: Exon boundaries on the architecture
cards.scientific_question: Where do this protein's internal coding-exon boundaries fall relative to its domain edges?
cards.interpretation: Generic exon-boundary classes, not the frozen FGFR2 Boundary Consistency vocabulary. Co-location of a boundary with a domain edge is positional.

cards.title: Signed boundary distances
cards.scientific_question: How far, and on which side, does each boundary sit from the nearest domain edge?
cards.interpretation: Distances are signed against the specific domain instance measured, so direction and domain identity are both preserved.

cards.title: Boundary-class summary
cards.scientific_question: How are this protein's exon boundaries distributed across the domain-relation classes?
cards.interpretation: Counts of mutually exclusive classes for one protein. Class membership depends on the near-edge threshold stated in the figure.

supplements.title: Framework overview
supplements.scientific_question: Which analysis steps produced the final isoform assignments?
supplements.interpretation: A methods diagram of the pipeline, not a result.

supplements.title: Exon-to-protein architecture (pre-InterPro)
supplements.scientific_question: How did coding exons project onto the proteins before the domain layer existed?
supplements.interpretation: Superseded by the all-species exon–domain architecture, which adds the domain layer to the same projection. Kept because the thesis cites it.

supplements.title: Label reconciliation and rescue summary
supplements.scientific_question: How many proteins needed their upstream label corrected or rescued?
supplements.interpretation: Counts of reconciliation outcomes. A rescued label is one supported by an external validated candidate, recorded per protein in the truth table.

supplements.title: Synteny review cases
supplements.scientific_question: Which loci did the synteny analysis flag for manual review?
supplements.interpretation: The flagged cases only. A flag marks a case worth inspecting, not an error.

supplements.title: All species · cassette zoom
supplements.scientific_question: How does the cassette region look in every protein of the panel?
supplements.interpretation: The per-protein form of the cassette zoom.

supplements.title: All species · exon-to-protein architecture
supplements.scientific_question: How do coding exons project onto every protein of the panel?
supplements.interpretation: The per-protein form of the pre-InterPro projection.

supplements.title: Full-length alignment · QC distributions
supplements.scientific_question: How are gap fraction and outlier scores distributed across the alignment?
supplements.interpretation: Distributions behind the alignment integrity figure.

supplements.title: Residue agreement · review cases
supplements.scientific_question: Which sequences disagreed with the human reference residues?
supplements.interpretation: The disagreeing cases only, for inspection.

supplements.title: Review cases
supplements.scientific_question: Which proteins carried a review flag before the InterPro step?
supplements.interpretation: Flagged proteins with the flag that was raised.

supplements.title: Review rows · cassette residue map
supplements.scientific_question: What do the cassette residues look like for the flagged rows?
supplements.interpretation: The residue map restricted to flagged rows.

supplements.title: Unresolved case panels
supplements.scientific_question: Which cases stayed unresolved, and what was seen for each?
supplements.interpretation: The unresolved cases with their recorded reason. An unresolved case is reported as unresolved and is not counted as a validated claim.

unavailable_combinations.omission_reason: no source-compatible validated candidate; sequence support only; the same protein is filed under this species' IIIc slot, so the two isoforms are not distinguishable by sequence here
no source-compatible validated candidate; sequence support only

availability.explanation: 30 species and 2 validated isoforms give 60 expected species-isoform combinations, of which 58 have an architecture model. The remaining 2 are combinations the freeze kept for review only; every species stays in the panel with the model or models it does have.

withdrawn_cards.title: Framework evidence stack
withdrawn_cards.reason: A per-protein QC view of which evidence layer set each final isoform label. It documents how the analysis reached its conclusions rather than answering a biological question, so it belongs to the validation record and not to the figure catalogue.

withdrawn_cards.title: Synteny neighbour conservation
withdrawn_cards.reason: Per-neighbour conservation cells over the same loci the main comparative Synteny neighbourhood figure already shows, where a blank cell is an annotation gap in one assembly rather than absence of the gene. The neighbourhood figure remains the catalogue's genomic-context card.

provenance.note: Rendered files are derived assets; a card is a scientific question. One card can own several rendered files as modes and export formats, and a file with no question behind it is not a card.
